public_requirement: outputs/analytic_posterior_grid.csv exists with exactly the header X,Z,alpha,beta,normed_exp_trans, exactly 40,000 data rows, all cells finite; every (X, Z) pair lies on the declared 0.01 grid within 1e-6 of its rounded hundredth, inside the declared ranges; the 40,000 declared cells are covered exactly once (coverage and multiplicity); alpha and beta strictly positive; normed_exp_trans finite, nonnegative, and summing to 1 within 1e-9.

The submitted grid agrees with an independent deterministic recomputation of the Part-1 posterior on the original task counts (read from the original-hash-checked input copy): alpha within 1e-9 relative, beta within 1e-9 relative, and normed_exp_trans within 1e-8 relative (plus a 1e-30 absolute floor) of the recomputed per-cell values; the weights sum to 1 within 1e-9. Cell alignment is by (X, Z) grid coordinates; row order is free, but arbitrary row order does not excuse missing, duplicated or out-of-range cells.

outputs/pymc_ab_posterior_draws.csv exists with exactly the header chain,draw,alpha,beta, exactly 8,000 data rows; alpha and beta finite and strictly positive; chain labels are exactly the distinct integers 1, 2, 3, 4 with exactly 2,000 rows per chain; within each chain the draw labels are the 2,000 distinct integers 0..1999; the 8,000 (alpha, beta) rows contain no exact duplicate rows. Row order is otherwise free (row identity is the draw, not its position).

The submitted retained draws must estimate the posterior of the exact Part-2 model (HalfNormal(10) priors on alpha and beta multiplied by the (alpha+beta)^(-5/2) hyperprior factor, theta marginalized analytically). Acceptance, measured on the submitted draw plain means and the pooled sample sds: the pooled draw means of alpha and beta must each lie within 2.5% relative of the exact posterior mean of the specified model (computed by numerical integration of that model on the supplied counts); the pooled sample sds within 20% relative of the exact posterior sds; the Pearson correlation between the alpha and beta draw columns within 0.15 of the exact posterior correlation; each chain's mean within 0.50 exact posterior sd of the pooled mean (both parameters). These are limits on observable output differences for this fixed sample size, not a guarantee that every wrong sampler configuration is detected; substantially biased samplers, wrong priors, truncated or padded chains fail them.

outputs/posterior_mean_estimates.csv exists with exactly the header method,parameter,estimate and exactly 4 data rows; the (method, parameter) labels are exactly the pairs (analytic_grid, alpha), (analytic_grid, beta), (pymc_mcmc, alpha), (pymc_mcmc, beta), each appearing exactly once; all fields non-missing; the estimate column numerically finite.

Each summary estimate must match the value derived from the submitter's own other files: analytic_grid rows equal the mass-weighted sums sum(alpha*normed_exp_trans) and sum(beta*normed_exp_trans) over the submitted grid, within 1e-10 relative (plus 1e-12 absolute); pymc_mcmc rows equal the plain arithmetic means of the submitted alpha and beta draw columns, within 1e-8 relative (plus 1e-10 absolute). Estimates must be reported at full available precision (rounding to a few decimals or other precision loss fails these tolerances; the deliberate Part-1 vs Part-2 prior difference is preserved and is not normalized away).
